content.overview: Section 30 permits the arbitral tribunal to encourage settlement of the dispute during arbitral proceedings. With the agreement of the parties, the tribunal may use mediation, conciliation or other procedures at any time during the proceedings; where settlement is reached, it may be recorded as an arbitral award on agreed terms in accordance with the section.
content.glance: Section 30 permits the arbitral tribunal to encourage settlement of the dispute during arbitral proceedings. With the agreement of the parties, the tribunal may use mediation, conciliation or other procedures at any time during the proceedings; where settlement is reached, it may be recorded as an arbitral award on agreed terms in accordance with the section.
content.study:
Module 1: Settlement encouragement
The tribunal may encourage settlement at any stage of the arbitral proceedings.

Module 2: Party agreement
With agreement of the parties, mediation, conciliation or other procedures may be used during the arbitration.

Module 3: Award on agreed terms
If the parties settle, the tribunal may record the settlement as an arbitral award on agreed terms where the statutory requirements are satisfied.

Module 4: Status of settlement award
An award on agreed terms has the statutory character of an arbitral award and is subject to the Act's regime, while the tribunal must not misdescribe a consensual settlement as an adjudicated merits determination.

examples.title: Rule applies
examples.body: Both parties agree to a settlement process during the arbitration and the tribunal records the final settlement as an award on agreed terms.

examples.title: Rule fails or changes
examples.body: The tribunal purports to impose a settlement on unwilling parties; section 30 facilitates consensual settlement and does not create a coercive settlement jurisdiction.

hypotheticals.question: Can the tribunal impose a settlement under section 30?
hypotheticals.analysis: No. Settlement through the mechanisms contemplated by section 30 is consensual; the tribunal may encourage settlement but does not obtain a power to compel agreement.

distinctions.title: Adjudicated award and award on agreed terms
distinctions.rows: Settlement embodied in an arbitral award on agreed terms.

misconceptions.trap: Assuming section 30 converts the tribunal into a compulsory mediator.
misconceptions.correction: The statutory function is to encourage settlement and, with party agreement, facilitate specified settlement procedures.

questionsAndAnswers.question: What is the purpose of section 30?
questionsAndAnswers.answer: It facilitates settlement during arbitration and permits a settlement to be recorded as an award on agreed terms when statutory requirements are met.

questionsAndAnswers.question: How should section 30 be applied in submissions?
questionsAndAnswers.answer: Start with the statutory text, identify every condition and then apply the facts to the precise statutory consequence.
questionsAndAnswers.explanation: Keep the submission statute-led and distinguish discretion, conditions and consequence.
